sentences.english: The good teacher calls the boys.
The boys hear the faithful teacher.
The teacher has a new book.
The boy sees the teacher's book.
And so the teacher praises the good boys.

sentences.latin: Nautae longum iter per magnum mare ad īnsulam faciunt.
sentences.english: The sailors make a long journey through the great sea to the island.

sentences.latin: Multae avēs in silvā altā audiuntur.
sentences.english: Many birds are heard in the tall forest.

sentences.latin: Nautae suīs amīcīs aquam et cibum dant.
sentences.english: The sailors give water and food to their own friends.

sentences.latin: Nautae piscēs magnōs in aquā capiunt.
sentences.english: The sailors catch big fish in the water.

sentences.latin: Itaque nautae fidēlēs īnsulam pulchram amant.
sentences.english: And so the faithful sailors love the beautiful island.

sentences.latin: Iūdex sapiēns et iūstus lēgēs veterēs cīvitātis magnae servat.
sentences.english: The wise and just judge preserves the old laws of the great state.

sentences.latin: Populus miser urbis magnae ā iūdice iūstō et sapientī regitur.
sentences.english: The wretched people of the great city are ruled by the just and wise judge.

sentences.latin: Vēritās lēgum ā iūdice praeclārō omnibus hominibus dīcitur.
sentences.english: The truth of the laws is spoken to all men by the illustrious judge.

sentences.latin: Itaque omnēs hominēs urbis vēritātem gravem iūdicis sapientis audiunt.
sentences.english: And so all the men of the city hear the weighty truth of the wise judge.

sentences.latin: Nam iūstus ōrdō cīvitātis lēgibus clārīs et veteribus mūnītur.
sentences.english: For the just order of the state is fortified by the clear and old laws.
